<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type
- Verdict: confirmed
- Confidence: high
- Severity: high
- Task type: correctness and production-safety adapter/workflow fix

### What Was Claimed
A structurally valid required local verification policy can name `npm test` even when the repository root has no matching npm script and the real package lives in a monorepo subdirectory. The failure is discovered only after a writer has committed changes.

### What We Found
The frozen implementation has three independent gaps:

1. `VerificationCommandPolicy` in `src/core/policy.ts` models only `argv`, `required`, and `timeoutMs`; the child runtime therefore has no trusted package-directory binding.
2. `/forge:init` in `src/ui/commands.ts` copies the root-oriented template without inspecting `package.json`, so it can generate an unusable required `npm test` command.
3. `ForgeWorkOnController.startIssue` in `src/workflows/work-on.ts` prepares and materializes the isolated writer worktree before any command feasibility check. There is no non-executing preflight for executable lookup, working-directory existence, package manifests, or npm script names.

`src/agents/child-runtime.ts` also executes approved commands with the worktree root as cwd, so adding a policy field must be propagated to the bound child and constrained to remain inside the assigned worktree. Existing verification result handling already distinguishes passed/failed/unknown and the merge gate remains fail-closed for required failures.

### Root Cause
The verification policy treats a command as a root-relative argv only and conflates command approval with command executability. Initialization does not derive policy from repository metadata, while work-on trusts the immutable policy without checking its filesystem/package preconditions before launching a writer.

### Affected Files
- `src/core/policy.ts` — validate and carry a relative `workingDirectory` for each approved command.
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` — add a read-only filesystem/PATH/npm-script preflight adapter.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — run preflight before worktree preparation or writer launch and provide exact remediation errors.
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` — bind and use the validated command working directory without permitting path escape.
- `src/adapters/subagents.ts` — preserve the new command field in the child binding.
- `src/ui/commands.ts` and `templates/config.json` — make init select only runnable npm scripts or explicitly emit a CI-only empty local command map.
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`, `test/core/policy.test.ts`, and relevant adapter/workflow tests — cover monorepo and fail-closed behavior.

### Evidence
- `parseForgePolicy` currently constructs command objects without any cwd/working-directory property.
- `/forge:init` copies `templates/config.json`; the template contains `npm test` with no package context.
- `startIssue` calls `#git.prepare` and `materializeForgeAgents` before `spawnWorkOn` and has no preflight call.
- `forge_verify` destructures argv and runs it with `cwd: root`.
- `test/core/policy.test.ts` and `test/adapters/subagents.test.ts` use root `npm test` fixtures; no test creates root-without-script plus package-with-script.

### History Findings
No additional history artifact or related implementation is available in the frozen worktree. The issue's reproduction is consistent with the current code and does not identify a duplicate implementation.

### Recommendation
Add a tracked, validated relative `workingDirectory` field (defaulting only if backward compatibility is explicitly retained), a non-executing preflight that checks every required local command's executable, directory, package manifest, and npm script, and invoke it before `prepare`/writer launch. Make `/forge:init` inspect package manifests and produce a runnable package-scoped command when one is selected; otherwise generate an explicit CI-only policy with no local commands. Propagate cwd through the immutable binding and use fail-closed path validation. Preserve post-implementation `forge_verify` exit handling and merge-gate rejection for genuine failures.

### Related Issues
- None found in the supplied issue context or frozen repository guidance.

### Decomposition Assessment
The change is coherent and can be implemented as one bounded policy, adapter, init, runtime, and regression-test update. No product or architecture decision is required if `workingDirectory` is a repository-relative path and empty commands remain the explicit CI-only mode.

### Acceptance Spec
- Validate repository-relative command working directories.
- Detect missing executables/directories/npm scripts without running repository scripts.
- Run required-command preflight before creating a writer worktree or spawning a writer.
- Report the exact `.forge/config.json` command path and `/forge:init`/config remediation.
- Let init select only a package that actually exposes the requested npm script, otherwise use explicit CI-only verification.
- Keep approved cwd in the child binding and preserve fail-closed verification results after implementation.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

No changes will be made to GitHub merge/close authority or post-implementation verification gate semantics.

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective
Prevent impossible required local verification policies from reaching a repository writer, while allowing safe monorepo package-scoped npm checks and preserving fail-closed post-implementation verification.

### Allowed Paths
- `src/core/policy.ts`
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts`
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`
- `src/adapters/subagents.ts`
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts`
- `src/ui/commands.ts`
- `templates/config.json`
- `test/core/policy.test.ts`
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`
- `test/adapters/subagents.test.ts`
- `test/fixtures/monorepo-no-root-test/package.json`
- `test/fixtures/monorepo-no-root-test/web/package.json`
- `README.md`
- `DESIGN.md`
- `SECURITY.md`

### Forbidden Changes
- Do not weaken GitHub identity, lease, state-journal, review, merge, issue-close, or cleanup authority.
- Do not execute repository npm scripts, arbitrary shell, or verification commands during preflight.
- Do not allow absolute or parent-traversing command working directories.
- Do not bypass the immutable child verification binding or alter required-check gate semantics.
- Do not add credentials, production data, or issue-body content to fixtures.
- Do not modify protected/default branch policy.

### Invariants
1. A verification command's `workingDirectory` is repository-relative, validated, and defaults to `.` only for legacy policies that omit it.
2. Preflight uses filesystem metadata, PATH lookup, and JSON parsing only; it never invokes the configured program or an npm lifecycle/script.
3. Every required local command is checked before `GitWorktreeManager.prepare`/writer launch; failures aggregate and identify the exact `.forge/config.json` command path plus `/forge:init` or config remediation.
4. An empty local command map explicitly means no local checks; GitHub CI remains responsible for verification.
5. The child runs a verified command from its bound package directory, with canonical path containment inside the assigned worktree.
6. Existing `forge_verify` status/exit-code behavior and merge-gate fail-closed handling remain unchanged.
7. `/forge:init` emits `npm test` only when a uniquely selected package manifest contains `scripts.test`; otherwise it emits an explicit CI-only empty command map.

### Deliverables
- Validated policy working-directory field and template representation.
- Read-only verification preflight adapter with executable, directory, package manifest, and npm-script checks.
- Work-on preflight call before any writer worktree/child launch.
- Propagated and contained package cwd in nested runtime bindings.
- Deterministic package-script discovery for `/forge:init`.
- Monorepo fixture and regression tests for passing package-scoped and failing root-scoped `npm test`.
- Documentation of package-scoped commands and CI-only mode.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### Callers and Data Flow
- `ForgeWorkOnController.startIssue` loads the trusted tracked policy, resolves the integration branch, and currently prepares/materializes/spawns. Insert preflight immediately after policy load and before `#git.prepare`.
- `SubagentsRpcClient.spawnWorkOn` serializes `policy.verification.commands` into the child binding. The new field must flow without a second mutable source.
- `forgeChildRuntime` validates binding data and `forge_verify` chooses the bound package cwd. Canonicalize and enforce worktree containment before `runProcess`.
- `/forge:init` copies the template, resolves repository identity, then writes the tracked config. Read package manifests before writing and remove the local test command when no unique runnable package is found.

### CI Surface
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` are repository verification commands in normal development, but the trusted run policy for this run has an empty local command map, so no `forge_verify` command is available. Verification will record that local checks are not configured; GitHub CI owns the required checks.
- Tests use Node's built-in test runner and temporary directories. New tests will inject PATH with a temporary executable and use filesystem APIs, not repository scripts.

### Prior Findings
- Issue #94's reproduction demonstrates root `npm test` failing in a monorepo after implementation because only argv was modeled.
- Current base code has no verification preflight adapter and no package-scoped cwd in policy/runtime.

### Hazards
- `workingDirectory` path escape through absolute, drive-qualified, `..`, or symlink paths.
- Treating `npm test` as valid without parsing the selected package's `scripts` object.
- Accidentally running npm during preflight.
- Selecting arbitrarily among multiple nested packages.
- Changing optional-check behavior or required verification gate semantics while adding preflight.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->
<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Extend policy parsing and the template with validated repository-relative `workingDirectory` (default `.` for backward compatibility); add focused policy assertions. Check IDs: `policy-cwd`, `policy-path-rejection`.
2. Implement `verification-preflight.ts`: discover uniquely selected package scripts for init; resolve executable via PATH/access; resolve and realpath working directories within the repository; parse package.json and verify npm `test`/`run` script names; aggregate required failures with exact config paths and remediation. Check IDs: `preflight-no-exec`, `preflight-missing-dir`, `preflight-missing-script`, `preflight-missing-executable`, `preflight-error-remediation`.
3. Invoke preflight before worktree preparation/writer launch and pass the existing trusted command map onward. Check IDs: `preflight-before-writer`, `ci-only-empty-policy`.
4. Propagate workingDirectory through subagent binding and enforce canonical assigned-worktree containment when running `forge_verify`. Check IDs: `binding-cwd`, `child-cwd-containment`, `required-failure-unchanged`.
5. Update `/forge:init` to choose a package only when `scripts.test` exists in exactly one candidate; otherwise generate CI-only commands, with fixture-backed tests. Check IDs: `init-runnable-selection`, `init-ci-only`.
6. Run the approved verification route if configured, inspect the final diff, commit, prepare the bound PR, and perform the required fresh correctness/security review. Check IDs: all above plus `review-gates`.

### Acceptance Mapping
- `policy-cwd`, `policy-path-rejection`, `binding-cwd`, `child-cwd-containment` → explicit validated working-directory field and safe runtime use.
- `init-runnable-selection`, `init-ci-only` → `/forge:init` never selects a missing npm test script and supports GitHub-CI-only output.
- `preflight-no-exec`, `preflight-missing-dir`, `preflight-missing-script`, `preflight-missing-executable`, `preflight-before-writer`, `preflight-error-remediation` → complete required-command preflight and actionable failure before writers.
- `required-failure-unchanged` → genuinely failed required post-implementation checks remain blocking.
- `review-gates` → no regression to review/merge authority.

### Out of Scope
- Discovering arbitrary CI commands beyond package metadata.
- Executing any verification check during `/forge:init` or preflight.
- Automatic changes to existing user-authored `.forge/config.json`.
- Replacing GitHub CI with local checks when no uniquely runnable package is discoverable.
- Changes to merge, close, cleanup, orchestration, or protected-branch behavior.

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
